title: 6 Ways Pride Blocks God’s Work in You
paragraphs: 6 Ways Pride Blocks God’s Work in You
There are people who still pray every day… but haven’t heard God clearly in years.
People who still attend church… still post Bible verses… still say “God is good”… while secretly feeling numb inside.
Not because the Holy Spirit stopped moving.
But because pride quietly built walls where surrender was supposed to live.
And the terrifying thing about pride is this:
Most proud people do not know they are proud.
Pride rarely walks into your life screaming.
But underneath all of it is the oldest poison humanity ever swallowed:
That was the serpent’s temptation in Eden.
The Hebrew language in Genesis reveals something chilling.
In Genesis 3:5, the serpent tells Eve:
Pride has always been the attempt to sit where only God belongs.
And some believers have no idea they are slowly turning their own opinions, emotions, ambitions, offenses, wounds, and desires into personal thrones.
“God resists the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.”
“To oppose.” “To set oneself against.” “To stand in battle formation against.”
Some people are praying for breakthrough while God Himself is opposing the pride they refuse to surrender.
That should shake every soul reading this.
Because pride does not merely slow spiritual growth.
Pride blocks God’s work in you.
And if we are honest… many of us have entertained forms of pride we baptized as personality.
This article is not written to condemn you.
It is written to expose what is silently suffocating your intimacy with God.
Because healing begins where honesty finally enters the room.
And maybe this is the moment God finally breaks something before it destroys you.
If this already feels uncomfortably personal… keep reading.
Someone you love desperately needs this too.
And before you keep going, be honest:
When was the last time you truly humbled yourself before God without defending yourself?
The first way pride blocks God’s work in you is by making correction feel like an attack.
Some people cannot be taught anymore.
The moment truth confronts them, walls go up.
Spiritual pride often reveals itself when correction arrives.
“Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates correction is stupid.”
The Hebrew word used there for “stupid” is:
It refers to someone spiritually senseless.
That sounds harsh because Scripture does not romanticize stubbornness.
God cannot transform someone who refuses correction.
Imagine asking the Great Physician to heal you while constantly denying the diagnosis.
Some people destroy relationships because they would rather protect their ego than protect love.
Some sabotage marriages because apologizing feels harder than losing the person.
Some stay spiritually stagnant for decades because admitting they were wrong feels unbearable.
“Lord… if I am wrong, expose me.”
After his sin with Bathsheba, he wrote in Psalm 51:17:
“The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.”
The Hebrew word for contrite is:
And some of you reading this are exhausted because you have been protecting an image instead of pursuing healing.
God cannot heal the version of you that keeps pretending.
The second way pride blocks God’s work in you is by making you depend on yourself more than God.
This is one of the most socially celebrated forms of pride.
“Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”
To rest your full weight upon.
Many believers claim to trust God while emotionally leaning entirely on themselves.
Humility trusts God even when understanding disappears.
This is why pride often produces chronic fear.
People trust their own limited understanding more than God’s eternal wisdom.
And eventually the weight crushes them.
“Apart from Me you can do nothing.”
“Separated from Me, you possess no power to accomplish anything.”
Some people only finally discover dependence on God after self-reliance destroys them.
The third way pride blocks God’s work in you is by making repentance feel unnecessary.
Because pride does not always deny sin.
That was literally the attitude Jesus condemned in the Pharisee.
“God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are.”
Meanwhile the tax collector beat his chest crying:
“God be merciful to me, a sinner.”
The Greek word for merciful there is:
The man knew he needed mercy.
And Jesus said that broken sinner went home justified before God.
There are people reading this who have mastered looking holy while slowly becoming spiritually numb.
God exposes what He still wants to heal.
The terrifying moment is not when conviction hurts.
The terrifying moment is when conviction disappears.
Because a seared conscience is one of the most dangerous places a soul can reach.
If God is still convicting you, He has not abandoned you.
The fourth way pride blocks God’s work in you is by making you crave recognition more than obedience.
Some people do “ministry” because they love visibility more than surrender.
Some worship publicly but rarely seek God privately.
Some want platforms more than prayer lives.
Jesus warned about this in Matthew 6.
He spoke about people who prayed publicly “to be seen by men.”
That hits hard in the social media generation.
Because pride can turn even spiritual things into performance.
But heaven is not impressed by image management.
And sometimes God will intentionally hide you before He can trust you.
Because obscurity exposes whether you truly love Him… or merely love being seen.
Some of the deepest spiritual growth happens in hidden seasons nobody applauds.
And many people abandon obedience when attention disappears.
“For if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ.”
You cannot worship approval and fully surrender to Jesus at the same time.
The fifth way pride blocks God’s work in you is by making forgiveness feel impossible.
Some people secretly believe their pain gives them permission to become bitter.
But unforgiveness slowly poisons the soul carrying it.
“Forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.”
The Greek word for forgiving is:
It comes from the word “charis,” meaning grace.
Biblical forgiveness is grace extended to the undeserving.
And some believers are asking God for peace while refusing to release bitterness.
Some people are spiritually suffocating because pride chained them to old wounds.
Forgiveness does not always erase pain instantly.
But it releases vengeance back into God’s hands.
“God, heal me enough that I stop drinking the poison of resentment.”
And maybe someone reading this has carried offense for years.
The prison of pride always feels justified while it destroys you slowly.
The sixth way pride blocks God’s work in you is by making surrender feel terrifying.
But faith requires surrender before clarity.
Abraham did not receive the full map.
Peter stepped onto water without certainty.
“Not my will, but Yours be done.”
The Greek word for will is:
Even Christ in His humanity surrendered fully to the Father.
That destroys the modern idol of self-will.
Because Christianity was never about inviting Jesus into your plans.
It was always about surrendering entirely to His.
“If any man would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.”
The Christian life is not self-exaltation.
And maybe the reason some people feel spiritually stuck is because God refuses to bless the version of them that still sits on the throne.
Some of you are exhausted trying to control outcomes God never asked you to carry.
Some are terrified to obey because surrender feels unsafe.
But the safest place a human being can live is fully surrendered to God.
Because pride promises protection while secretly isolating you from the very presence that gives life.
Jesus did not merely come to forgive pride.
He came to crush its power.
The King of Glory humbled Himself to the point of death on a cross.
The sinless One lowered Himself to save rebels.
That is the opposite of pride.
And because of Jesus, transformation is possible.
Grace still reaches people who finally surrender.
That is the beauty of the Gospel.
God is not searching for impressive people.
He is searching for surrendered hearts.
And maybe tonight God is exposing pride not to shame you… but to free you.
Because the moment humility enters, grace rushes in.
That is where intimacy with God returns.
That is where chains finally break.
If this article convicted you deeply, do not ignore it.
Send this to someone who needs a spiritual wake-up call.
One day you will realize God was not trying to destroy your pride to humiliate you… He was trying to remove the chains keeping you from becoming who He created you to be.
